name: Skewed Memory Organization for Conflict-Free Ray Access
aliases: Skewed Memory Organization with Barrel Shifting
definition: A memory organization scheme for a Cubic Frame Buffer (CFB) of $n^3$ voxels divided into $n$ memory banks, each holding $n^2$ voxels, designed to allow simultaneous conflict-free access to a full ray of $n$ voxels in one memory cycle, accessing only one voxel from each bank.
summary: Skewed memory organization maps 3D voxel data into memory banks using modular arithmetic to ensure conflict-free simultaneous ray access, distinguishing itself from standard layouts by enabling efficient parallel retrieval and geometric transformations.
